'''Marius Sudol''' is an American molecular and cellular biologist.  He was born in 1954 in Tarnow, Poland. In 1978, he immigrated to the United States to study at The Rockefeller University in New York City,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hR1NGUeY3G0C&q=Marius+Sudol+Rockefeller&pg=PA1825|title=The Rockefeller University » Book reference to Rockefeller|year=1988}}</ref> where he received his Ph.D. in 1983.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.huck.psu.edu/event/to-be-announced-5|title=Event: to be announced 5 - The Huck Institutes|website=www.huck.psu.edu}}</ref> He is currently an Adjunct Faulty at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in NYC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mountsinai.org/profiles/marius-sudol|title=Marius Sudol &#124; Mount Sinai - New York|website=Mount Sinai Health System}}</ref>

== Research ==
Sudol's research was mainly focused on cell signaling, oncogenes, and mechanobiology.<ref name="mbi.nus.edu.sg">{{cite web|author= |url=https://mbi.nus.edu.sg/marius-sudol/ |title=Marius Sudol – Mechanobiology Institute, National University of Singapore |publisher=Mbi.nus.edu.sg |date= 25 April 2016|accessdate=2021-02-22}}</ref> The key goal of his research team has been to understand signaling modalities of WW domain-containing YAP (aka YAP1) oncoprotein and crosstalk of other WW domain-containing proteins in the Hippo-YAP/TAZ tumor suppressor pathway.<ref name="mbi.nus.edu.sg"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genecards.org/cgi-bin/carddisp.pl?gene=YAP1|title=YAP1 Gene - GeneCards &#124; YAP1 Protein &#124; YAP1 Antibody|website=www.genecards.org}}</ref> He is known for his work on modular protein domains.<ref>{{Cite journal|pmid = 11163176|year = 2000|last1 = Sudol|first1 = M.|last2 = Hunter|first2 = T.|title = NeW wrinkles for an old domain|journal = Cell|volume = 103|issue = 7|pages = 1001–4|doi = 10.1016/s0092-8674(00)00203-8|s2cid = 18274171|doi-access = free}}</ref> Among his 180 published papers, he has a number of highly cited articles, which have been referenced collectively more than 18,000 times.<ref name="scholar.google.com">{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=7fLNOt0AAAAJ&hl=en|title=Marius Sudol|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> His [[H-index]] is 83.<ref name="scholar.google.com"/>

== Career and service ==
Besides his academic affiliations in the US and Singapore,<ref name="mbi.nus.edu.sg"/> Sudol served in the Scientific Advisory Board of AxCell-Cytogen company from 2000 - 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.genomeweb.com/axcell-mount-sinai-study-protein-pathways-neurodegenerative-disorders|title=AxCell, Mount Sinai to Study Protein Pathways of Neurodegenerative Disorders|website=GenomeWeb|date=15 November 2001 }}</ref> and was a co-founder and co-leader of the Protein Modules Consortium from 2003 - 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.proteinmodules.org/home|title=Protein Modules Consortium|website=www.proteinmodules.org}}</ref> From 2016 to 2019, he taught at The Beutler Institute in Xiamen University, China.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tbi.xmu.edu.cn/5105/list.htm|title=Core Course Lecturers|website=tbi.xmu.edu.cn}}</ref>

*Klingenstein Award in the Neurosciences (1991-1994)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.klingfund.org|title=The Esther A. & and Joseph Klingenstein Fund, Inc.|last=University|first=The Rockefeller|website=www.klingfund.org|access-date=2018-08-20}}</ref>
